parameters.query:
-- Azure Synapse / SQL Server version
WITH w AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM bookymyshow.bookings_fact
  WHERE booking_time >= DATEADD(day, -7, SYSUTCDATETIME())
)
SELECT
  'Last 7 Days' AS period,
  COUNT(*) AS total_transactions,
  SUM(total_amount) AS total_revenue,
  AVG(total_amount) AS avg_transaction_value,
  COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS unique_customers,
  SUM(CASE WHEN payment_status = 'Success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) AS success_rate_pct,

  SUM(CASE WHEN event_category LIKE '%Music%'  THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END) AS music_revenue,
  SUM(CASE WHEN event_category LIKE '%Cinema%' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END) AS cinema_revenue,
  SUM(CASE WHEN event_category LIKE '%Sports%' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sports_revenue,

  SUM(CASE WHEN booking_platform = 'Mobile App' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS mobile_bookings,
  SUM(CASE WHEN booking_platform = 'Website'   THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS website_bookings,

  (SELECT TOP 1 customer_city
     FROM w
     WHERE customer_city IS NOT NULL
     GROUP BY customer_city
     ORDER BY SUM(total_amount) DESC) AS top_city,

  SUM(CASE WHEN alert_category <> 'Normal' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS anomaly_count,
  AVG(processing_time_ms) AS avg_processing_time_ms
FROM w;

parameters.text:
=You will receive a JSON payload with:
- period: string (e.g., "Last 7 Days")
- generated_at: human-friendly timestamp
- metrics: object with keys like:
  total_revenue, total_transactions, avg_transaction_value, unique_customers,
  success_rate_pct, top_city, anomaly_count, avg_processing_time_ms,
  music_revenue, cinema_revenue, sports_revenue, mobile_bookings, website_bookings
- highlights: optional object (e.g., top_category, top_platform)
- raw: same keys but not always needed

Here is the JSON payload:
{{ JSON.stringify($json, null, 2) }}

Please produce ONE JSON object with fields subject, preheader, html as per the system instructions.

Email body (html) requirements:
1) Title: “BookMyShow Weekly Business Report”
2) Subheader line: “Period: {{ $json.period }}  •  Generated: {{ $json.generated_at }}”
3) Metrics table (2 columns: Metric | Value). Include at least:
   - Total Revenue (₹ with two decimals)
   - Transactions
   - Unique Customers
   - Success Rate (%)
   - Avg Transaction (₹ with two decimals)
   - Top City
   - Anomalies
   - Avg Proc Time (ms)
4) Section “Revenue by Top Category”. Show each (₹ with two decimals). 
5) Show counts and a brief 1-line takeaway for top platform distribtuion.
6) Section “Analyst Notes”: 3–4 concise bullet points highlighting what leadership should know (e.g., growth drivers, risks, actions).

Styling:
- Wrap content in a <div style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#222;max-width:680px;margin:0 auto">
- Tables: border-collapse:collapse; borders #eee; td padding 8px; left-aligned labels; right-aligned values
- Headings with modest margins (e.g., h2 margin:0 0 8px; h3 margin:18px 0 8px)
- No remote assets, no images, no CSS classes, all inline styles.

Output JSON, nothing else.

messageValues.message: =You are a senior business analyst. Write leadership-ready weekly emails with a crisp, confident tone. ALWAYS return a single JSON object that matches this exact shape:  {   "subject": "string",   "preheader": "string",   "html": "string" }  Rules: - Do NOT include markdown or code fences. No backticks. Return raw JSON only. - Use inline CSS only (no <style> blocks, no remote fonts). - Use a clean two-column table for metrics with subtle borders (#eee) and padding (6–8px). - Format INR money using the Indian grouping style (₹81,857.97 → keep two decimals). - Avoid external images; everything must be plain HTML. - Keep the subject compact and informative (e.g., “BookMyShow Weekly — ₹81,858 revenue, 52 tx”). - Preheader is a short one-liner (will appear in email preview). - Keep the email width comfortable (max 680px). - Do not echo the input JSON.
